scene: Beatrice gives Dante a prophetic charge; Matelda brings Dante and Statius to Eunoe, and its restorative water completes Purgatorio
story: The seven women lament the chariot's loss with the opening of Psalm 79, 'Deus, venerunt gentes'. Beatrice responds with the words 'Modicum, et non videbitis me; et iterum, modicum, et vos videbitis me', and leads Dante onward with the women and sages.

Beatrice foretells that the corrupted chariot and its captor will not remain unchallenged. She invokes a mysterious 'five hundred, ten and five' (DXV) who will defeat the giant and the woman. The cryptic figure is a prophecy within the poem, not an event Dante witnesses.

Beatrice commands Dante to remember what he has seen and report it faithfully when he returns to the living, even though he does not yet fully understand her allegory. Dante admits his difficulty comprehending her words.
They reach another clear spring and stream. Beatrice directs Matelda to guide Dante to Eunoe, whose function is to restore the memory of good deeds. Statius accompanies Dante.
Matelda brings Dante to Eunoe and gives him the restorative water. Having drunk both Lethe and Eunoe, Dante is renewed, like young plants newly clothed with leaves, and ready to rise to the stars.

The thirty-three cantos of Purgatorio conclude. The seven P marks remain zero; Lethe and Eunoe have both been performed. Paradiso begins next; the completed ascent and earlier Inferno remain sealed as provenance.

semanticSomatic.semantic: A symbolic account can be entrusted to a witness without pretending all its elements are already understood
Faithful witness remembers the message; the second water restores positive memory and readiness for the next journey
The previously pending water is administered to complete a distinct restorative operation
Restoration of remembered goodness follows Lethe's completed release of sinful memory

witnesses.observable: the second memory operation now occurs rather than remaining promised

witnesses.action: WITNESS Dante's renewal and his stated READINESS to rise to the stars
witnesses.observable: Purgatorio ends, both waters performed, seven P marks remain cleared

alchemicalReading: The final vessel does not erase history. Lethe releases remembrance of sin; Eunoe restores the memory of good. After the witnessed second rite, readiness is asserted in the poem and the complete thirty-three-canto ascent can be sealed as a new milestone.
invariant: Eunoe is marked performed only after Dante actually drinks it in XXXIII. Lethe remains performed from XXXI; zero P marks remain; Beatrice's DXV prophecy is attributed speech, not independently verified future history.
